text:
sarah: Heads-up — Nightingale (customer) opened a support ticket: p99 doubled and overall throughput ~50% down starting ~03:05 UTC. Support attached a few traces and a short timeline. Can someone grab profiling + quick checks? https://redwood/support/INC-4532

raj: On it. Any known deploys around 03:00–03:15?

kelly: I promoted kernel-selector-v2 to prod at 03:08; small rollout (10%). I saw mild queueing in staging after the config change but nothing major. Can rollback if needed. :frowning:

perf-bot: Deployment kernel-selector-v2 to prod succeeded (id:depl-9123) — 03:08 UTC

mike: Starting capture now. Running: 
```
rdwctl collect-profile --service=nightingale --span=180 --format=pprof --out=/tmp/ng_prof_2119876543.pb
```
I'll also grab flamegraphs and top.

kelly: Quick metric checks: can someone confirm KV cache hit rate and inflight requests? Example query: 
```
curl -s "http://metrics.internal/api/series?name=kv_cache_hit_rate&service=nightingale" | jq .
```
If hit rate dropped, could explain token regen and backend pressure.

raj: I pulled the trace bundle that support attached. Lots of requests with seq_len>2048 after 03:05. Looks like customer started a bulk job. That would increase KV cache pressure and cause more backend fetches.

support: Confirmed — Nightingale ran a migration-style batch at 03:04 that fans out many long-context calls. They didn't expect this to overlap with peak. We're coordinating with them to throttle.

mike: Uploading initial flamegraph: /tmp/ng_flame_2119876543.svg (shared in the ticket). Top hotspot is attention_kv_fetch and rpc_fetch_backend. Sample from runtime.log: 
```
[03:09:12] runtime: request=tx-83a2 seq_len=4096 model=gptx-large
[03:09:12] runtime: queue_wait_ms=1200 kernel=kernel-selector-v2
[03:09:12] rpc: backend_fetch_ms=980 host=10.2.3.45
[03:09:13] runtime: finished request=tx-83a2 status=200 tokens=2300
```

raj: That queue_wait spike + backend_fetch ~1s lines up with p99 bump. Two likely contributors: (1) sudden long-ctx burst from customer, (2) kernel-selector rollout causing slightly higher queueing under burst.

kelly: Agree. Since rollout is small, we can pause/rollback to be safe. If rollback ROI low, we should tune admission/batching thresholds for long-ctx.

sarah: Action items: 1) Support will ask Nightingale to throttle the batch by 2x (support). 2) mike to keep collecting pprof + flamegraphs for next 30m. 3) raj/kelly to decide rollback by 03:40 UTC if p99 doesn't improve. 4) postmortem note in the ticket with recommended limits.

raj: I'll watch p99 dashboards (ng-service.p99) and post an update here. If I don't post by 03:40 I'll assume rollback and take it.

mike: profile finished, uploaded to ticket. Initial comparison shows KV hit rate fell from 0.96 -> 0.62 during the window.

support: Nightingale agrees to throttle now; they reduced concurrency by 3x at 03:22 UTC. Monitoring.

kelly: rolling kernel-selector-v2 back from 10% -> 0% now (started). Will report when rollback done.

perf-bot: Rollback of deployment kernel-selector-v2 initiated (id:depl-9123-rollback) — 03:26 UTC

raj: p99 trending down to baseline after throttle + rollback. Looks like both changes helped. I'll keep the ticket open for a postmortem and recommend a default long-ctx admission cap for customers.

sarah: Thanks all. Please add short notes to INC-4532 and tag @oncall for follow-up tomorrow (tuning admission+batching). :thumbsup:
